about.title: From interfaces to products
paragraphs: Hi, I’m Karol, a Product Designer with nearly 10 years in design and almost 7 in UX/UI and front-end development.

I’ve designed B2B platforms, web and mobile apps across mobility and banking, often for complex, data-heavy products where clarity really matters. I care a lot about design systems, accessibility and the small details that make an interface feel consistent.
And because I also code, I design with development in mind: interfaces that look good, and actually get built the way they were designed.

interfaceWebApp.seoTitle: Interface Web App — Flexis case study · Karol Giraldo
interfaceWebApp.seoDescription: UX/UI case study: Flexis Interface, a web platform built from scratch to turn fleet data into clear decisions.

hero.title:
From fleet data to
clear daily decisions
hero.lead: A web platform built from scratch to help fleet managers make sense of their data and prioritize their actions.
hero.videoLabel: Screen recording of the Flexis Interface dashboard: fleet availability, mileage consumption, alerts and a live map of vehicles.

problem.title: The problem
problem.lead: Location, battery, maintenance, availability: there was no shortage of data. What was missing was knowing where to start.
problem.detail: Managers switched between tools, often ended up in Excel, and reacted to problems instead of anticipating them.

solution.title: The solution
solution.lead: A platform that brings fleet data together and organizes it by priority, so managers know what to handle first and how to act.

cards.title: Fleet Overview
cards.text: What needs attention today, at a glance.
cards.alt: Flexis Interface home dashboard: fleet availability, mileage consumption, alerts requiring attention and a map of vehicles on route.

cards.title: Vehicle detail
cards.alt: Vehicle detail screen: check-in and check-out, monthly mileage, annual consumption, battery level and vehicle location.

cards.title: Actionable workflows
cards.text: From alert to action in a few steps.
cards.alt: Notification Center with the list of fleet alerts and an open panel for a low tire pressure alert, with the recommended action.

context.label: (Context)
context.title: Fleet management is becoming increasingly complex.
context.lead: Fleet managers now have to deal with a growing volume of data, varied business needs and increasingly complex operations. Against this backdrop, Flexis set out to build a new platform to centralize information and simplify day-to-day management.

research.title: Research
research.lead: Fleet tools show what’s happening, but not what to do about it.
research.text: Interviews with fleet management experts, along with a review of tools like Geotab and Samsara, pointed to three gaps.
research.conclusion: The result: managers bounce between tools and end up piecing everything together in Excel.

gaps.text: No clear priorities: everything is tracked and reported, but nothing shows what needs attention first.
gaps.alt: Fleet dashboard widgets side by side: a driving smoothness score chart, 10% of vehicles charging and 1 of 10 charge points in use.

gaps.text: Scattered information: vehicles, drivers and charging are managed in separate tools.
gaps.alt: An electric van surrounded by separate cards: a wallbox at the Lyon hub with two available charge points, and 3 of 10 charge points available.

gaps.text: Built for one role: most solutions are designed solely for the fleet manager.
gaps.alt: Role picker with Fleet Manager selected; the other roles, Dispatcher, Fleet Advisor and Financial Manager, fade into the background.

fleetAdvisor.title: Fleet Advisor
fleetAdvisor.text: Provides advice and support on fleet strategy

financialManager.title: Financial Manager
financialManager.text: Oversees financial planning for the fleet

question.text: How might we turn a large amount of <muted>fragmented fleet data</muted> into a simple experience that helps teams know what to do next?

process.title: Process
process.lead: With no existing product, every module was shaped around a business goal.

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: Interviews with business experts and benchmarking to define each module before designing it.
steps.alt: A fleet advisor in a high-visibility vest holding a tablet, in front of a board about monthly on-site visits.

steps.title: Define
steps.text: With the Product and Business teams, priority features were selected and the journeys for the first version defined.
steps.alt: Workshop board with priorities ranked high, medium and low, the problem statement, hypotheses and research goals.

steps.title: Design & validate
steps.text: Wireframes reviewed with developers, business experts and beta testers before moving to high-fidelity UI.
steps.alt: Meeting room with the User Management screen projected on a large screen during a review session.

slides.title: Not all data carries the same weight.

items.title: Audit
items.text: An inventory of all available data: vehicles, telematics and operations.

items.title: Prioritize
items.text: Information ranked by urgency and required action, to separate what informs from what needs intervention.

items.title: Structure
items.text: Three levels of detail: the fleet overview, the vehicle detail, then the action to take.

slides.alt: Flexis screens layered on top of each other: the fleet management table, the filter panel and a vehicle detail page with mileage and consumption.

slides.title: A design system built alongside the product.
slides.text: With no existing interface to build on, the design system was created at the same time as the product. Recurring elements (statuses, alerts, filters, actions) became reusable components: the same information always looks and behaves the same way, and new modules don’t add complexity to the experience.
slides.alt: Design system components: buttons, checkbox, KPI cards, alerts, status tags and a mileage progress bar with a warning.

final.title: Final Thoughts

stats.label: product modules designed end to end

final.summary: A platform that brings fleet data together and helps managers know what to handle first, built from scratch and ready for development.
final.photoAlt: A fleet manager in a high-visibility vest working at her desk, with the Flexis planning screen on her monitor.

driverApp.seoTitle: Driver App — Flexis case study · Karol Giraldo
driverApp.seoDescription: UX/UI case study: Flexis Driver App, a mobile app built from scratch to make urban delivery drivers’ days easier.

hero.title:
From vehicle pickup
to mission done, in
one app
hero.lead: A mobile app built from scratch to make urban delivery drivers’ days easier, from vehicle pickup to the end of their route.
hero.videoLabel: Screen recording of the Flexis Driver App: finding the assigned vehicle on a map and starting navigation to it.

problem.title: The problem
problem.lead: Drivers switched between multiple tools every day, with no easy way to register which vehicle they were driving.
problem.detail: Vehicles were tracked live in Interface, but there was no reliable way to know who was driving each one, or when.

solution.title: The solution
solution.lead: An app that brings every step of a driver’s day into one place, from vehicle pairing to the end of the route.

cards.title: Vehicle pairing
cards.text: Scan the QR code or enter the VIN number to start a mission, or unlock the vehicle with a virtual key.
cards.alt: Vehicle pairing screen: the camera scans the vehicle’s VIN number, with a field to enter the vehicle code manually.

cards.title: Video check-in & check-out
cards.text: The driver films the vehicle, and an integrated inspection service completes the report.
cards.alt: The driver films the vehicle, and an integrated inspection service generates the report.

cards.title: Optimized routes
cards.text: Stop order and routes planned to save time and energy.
cards.alt: Mission navigation screen: turn-by-turn directions on a night map, the next stop and buttons to call the customer or report an incident.

context.label: (Context)
context.title: Urban delivery: tight schedules and shared vehicles.
context.lead: In urban delivery, drivers often share the same vehicles, schedules are tight, and electric vans add a new constraint: range. Flexis built this app for delivery drivers across Europe.

research.title: Discovery
research.lead: Fleet management tools know where every vehicle is, but they weren’t designed for the drivers behind the wheel.
research.text: Workshops with the product team and business experts brought three gaps in drivers’ day-to-day work to light:
research.conclusion: The result: low driver engagement and a less productive fleet.

gaps.text: Scattered tools: drivers managed their deliveries across several tools, with no real-time information.
gaps.alt: An electric van between three status cards: vehicle not connected, vehicle connected and ready to check in, and vehicle ready to start the day.

gaps.text: Missing the basics: existing solutions offered neither a simple sign-up nor secure vehicle access.
gaps.alt: The Driver App home screen with turn-by-turn directions, a van seen from above and a “Find Your Vehicle” card.

gaps.text: No driver–vehicle pairing: there was no simple way to link a driver to a vehicle at the start of the day.
gaps.alt: An electric van in front of a “Find Your Vehicle” card and a link icon.

question.text: How might we simplify drivers’ days with a <muted>single app</muted>, from vehicle access to the end of their route, while making sure every trip is linked to the right driver?

process.title: Process
process.lead: No existing product: every module started from a business goal.

steps.title: Map
steps.text: Story mapping turned business goals into epics and user stories, from driver sign-up to route tracking.
steps.alt: Story mapping board for mission planning, with the user needs, the vehicle types and the unassigned routes.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.text: With the Product and Business teams, the essential features were set for the first release, and the rest planned for later.
steps.alt: A designer arranging sticky notes on a glass wall, under the steps of the driver’s journey: profile, vehicle, location, stats and planning.

steps.title: Design & validate
steps.text: User flows and low-fidelity mockups, validated before development began.
steps.alt: A driver in a high-visibility vest holding a phone with the Driver App’s “Session Completed” screen.

slides.title: Everything starts with vehicle pairing.
paragraphs: A driver’s day begins as soon as they’re paired with a vehicle, by QR code, VIN or virtual key. From there, the app guides them step by step:
Pairing → Check-in → Ready to go → Route → Check-out
For the driver, it’s one simple step. For the fleet manager, it’s how they know who drove each vehicle, and when.
slides.alt: Screen recording of the Driver App scanning a van’s VIN number to assign the driver to the vehicle, with a field to enter the code manually.

slides.title: Route planning that saves time and battery.
paragraphs: The app sets the order of stops and suggests routes based on travel time and the vehicle’s charge level, so drivers can finish their route faster without worrying about running out of range.
slides.alt: Route screens of the Driver App: a night map with the suggested route, the list of the day’s 12 stops with their times, and the next customer with buttons to call them or report an incident.

slides.title: A simpler, faster vehicle inspection.
paragraphs: At check-in and check-out, the driver just films the vehicle. An integrated inspection service turns the video into a condition report and sends it straight to the fleet manager.
slides.alt: Video check-in screen: the driver films the van from the outside, next to a “Start Check-in” card and warning and inspection icons.

slides.title: One design system for both products, adapted to life on the road.
paragraphs: The driver app shares the same foundations as the web platform (design tokens, components and icons), adapted for use on the move: larger touch targets for use in the cab, simpler screens to reduce cognitive load on the road, and both light and dark themes.
slides.alt: Three Driver App screens in light and dark mode: the home screen with the vehicle tools, the settings with the theme picker, and the van’s battery at 75%.

final.title: Final Thoughts
final.statement: From a product framework to a dev-ready MVP.

stats.label: driver journeys designed end to end

final.summary: An app that supports drivers from vehicle pickup to the end of their route, built from scratch and ready for development.
final.photoAlt: A delivery driver in a high-visibility vest smiling at his phone, which shows the Driver App with the van’s battery at 75%, in front of an electric van.

creditMutuelCic.seoTitle: Crédit Mutuel & CIC — CSS framework redesign · Karol Giraldo
creditMutuelCic.seoDescription: UI & front-end case study: redesign of the CSS framework behind the Crédit Mutuel and CIC client area, aligning it with the group’s new brand guidelines.

hero.title:
Bringing the client area
in line with the group’s
new brand identity.
hero.lead: The redesign of the CSS framework and components behind Crédit Mutuel and CIC online banking.
hero.videoLabel: Screen recording of the redesigned online banking login page: the sign-in form with its new inputs and buttons.

problem.title: The problem
problem.lead: The group rolled out a new brand identity across all its channels. For the client area, the challenge was to apply it to a very large number of pages, using a CSS framework built for the previous brand guidelines.

solution.title: The solution
solution.lead: A new version of the CSS framework, with components updated to the new brand guidelines and reusable across the entire client area.*

cards.title: 20+ components updated
cards.text: to reflect the new brand guidelines.
cards.alt: Components of the client area redesigned with the new identity, shown with a fictional brand.

cards.title: One framework for both brands
cards.text: The same components adapt to the Crédit Mutuel and CIC identities.
cards.alt: The same components themed for two fictional brands from one shared codebase.

cards.title: Modular, reusable components
cards.text: A shared foundation for every team building client area journeys.
cards.alt: Several client-area pages assembled from the same reusable components, shown with a fictional brand.

intro.note: *Confidential project: the components shown were recreated from the two banks’ public brand guidelines and displayed under fictional names. Further details available on request.

context.label: (Context)
context.title: 90% of the framework’s components are used in the client area.
context.lead: Account overview, loans, messages with an advisor: most journeys available after login rely on these components. Rolling out the group’s new brand identity therefore meant modernizing them.

bank.alert: Your new card is on its way.

message.text: Your loan simulation is ready. Shall we go over it on Thursday?

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.lead: Too many pages to redesign one by one.
challenge.text: The framework already existed, but it had been built for the previous brand identity. Applying the new design on top of it meant overriding styles page after page, adding complexity with every change.

gaps.text: A huge client area: a large number of internal pages, built by different teams.
gaps.alt: A stack of grey page wireframes fading into the background, with a new message from the advisor and a current account line, among small icon buttons.

gaps.text: Two brands, one codebase: Crédit Mutuel and CIC share the same components, each with its own visual identity.
gaps.alt: The same amount field and button in a neutral grey version, linked by thin lines to two branded versions: Banque Alpha and Banque Beta.

gaps.text: Overrides everywhere: every new style had to fight the old one, making the code harder to maintain.
gaps.alt: A dark code editor with Less code for a button: the old properties are crossed out and the new ones only win with !important, with a warning: 12 overrides on .btn.

question.text: How might <muted>we modernize our framework</muted> so the new identity works everywhere, without <muted>overriding the old styles</muted>?

built.title: The approach
built.lead: Rather than duplicating every component for each brand, the framework relies on a single neutral base, with variables carrying the visual identity of Crédit Mutuel and CIC.

slides.title: Components aligned with the new brand guidelines
slides.text: The colors, shapes and styles of each component were derived from the public website mockups. The page structure was left unchanged: in a banking group, any structural change involves long validation cycles.
slides.alt: A fictional public website mockup on the left; on the right, the colors, button shape and typography derived from it, and the resulting button.

slides.title: A neutral default theme
slides.text: Every component is built on an internal visual identity, independent of Crédit Mutuel and CIC. All its properties are variables, so adapting it to either brand simply means changing their values.
slides.alt: A table of variables: primary color, corner radius, figures font and button, each shown for the Default, Banque Alpha and Banque Beta themes.

slides.title: Shared styles, written once
slides.text: Recurring styles were grouped into Less mixins and reused across all components, making the code lighter and easier to maintain.
slides.alt: A Less code editor with a button mixin written once and used by a primary and a secondary button, shown next to the two resulting buttons.

slides.title: Tested and validated with every service
slides.text: Since the new version also changed the framework’s internal structure, every update was tested and validated with the services that use it.
slides.alt: An acceptance checklist of the services using the framework, four validated and one in review, above the steps test, iterate and acceptance.

final.title: Final Thoughts
final.statement: From a new brand to every page behind the login.
final.summary: A modernized CSS framework that brings the group’s new brand identity to the entire client area, and provides a flexible foundation for future sites.
final.photoAlt: A fictional banking screen that switches between the Default, Banque Alpha and Banque Beta themes: the same account card, field and button with different colors and shapes.
